marking_points.point: Anomaly detection predicts future events from events that have already occurred using rules.

marking_points.point: A limitation of anomaly detection is that intrusion scenarios not described by the rules will not be flagged.
marking_points.quote: The problem is that some intrusion scenarios that are not described by the rules will not be flaged intrusive.

marking_points.point: An advantage of anomaly detection is that systems built on this model are highly adaptive to changes.

accepted.question: State the Chinese Wall policy and explain its simple security rule and its *-property. Then explain why this policy is described as addressing a specialised concern and how its permissions differ from static access rights.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy was proposed by Brewer and Nash to address conflicts of interest.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash (1989) proposed a policy called the Chinese Wall Policy that addresses such conflicts of interest.

marking_points.point: It is an access control confidentiality policy rather than an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: Under the simple security rule, a subject may access an object only if it is within the Wall (same company datasets already accessed) or in an entirely different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s, that is, "within the Wall," or
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote covers the 'within the Wall' condition but omits the alternative 'entirely different conflict of interest class' part of the rule.

marking_points.point: The *-property permits a write only when the simple security rule also allows the access and the subject cannot read any unsanitized object belonging to a different company dataset than the one being written to.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

marking_points.point: The policy is designed for a very specific concern: conflicts of interest faced by a consultant or contractor.
marking_points.quote: Unlike previous policies, Brewer and Nash's Chinese Wall Policy is designed to address a very specific concern: conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor.

marking_points.point: Permissions change dynamically, since access rights depend on the history of past accesses.
marking_points.quote: Notice that permissions change dynamically. The access rights that any subject enjoys depends on the history of past accesses

questions.question: Compare how a misuse detection system and an anomaly detection system each classify activity as an attack, and explain one limitation of each approach when used as a countermeasure against threats.

marking_points.quote: there are ways to represent attacks in the form of a pattern or a signature so that even variations of the same attack can be detected

marking_points.point: Misuse detection recognises known bad behaviour rather than unknown behaviour.

marking_points.point: A limitation of misuse detection is that it is of little use against unknown attack methods.
marking_points.quote: They can detect many or all known attack patterns, but they are of little use for unknown attack methods.

marking_points.point: Anomaly detection predicts future events from events that have already occurred using rules.

marking_points.point: A limitation of anomaly detection is that intrusion scenarios not described by the rules will not be flagged.

marking_points.point: An advantage of anomaly detection is that systems built on this model are highly adaptive to changes.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Trojans disguise themselves as useful or benign programs so that users accept them.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that Trojans masquerade as helpful or harmless programs, matching the point about disguising as useful or benign programs.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: An executable can be infected by overwriting its header so that the entry point is redirected to the virus.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states overwriting a program header to switch the entry point to a virus, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Early malware such as Elk Cloner spread by infecting the boot sector.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms boot sector infection as a spreading method but does not mention Elk Cloner or early malware specifically.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The Morris worm propagated across the Arpanet by exploiting a debugging feature of sendmail for remote execution.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms the sendmail debugging feature for remote execution but does not mention the Morris worm or Arpanet propagation.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Windows includes a Security Reference Monitor operating in kernel mode that performs ACL verification.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms the Security Reference Monitor performs ACL verification but does not state it operates in kernel mode.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Malware can cause unauthorized disclosure of information, which is a breach of confidentiality.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that disclosure is unauthorized access to information, matching the confidentiality breach described in the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Malware can compromise integrity by modifying data without authorization.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote mentions modification and integrity services countering it, but does not explicitly state that malware causes unauthorized data modification.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: It obtained the list of a user's heroes by issuing a GET request on a user profile.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states the point that the list of a user's heroes was obtained via a GET on a user profile.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Any visitor to an infected user's page had their own profile and friends list infected, so the worm spread from page to page.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that any visitor to an infected user's page gets their profile and friends list infected, matching the point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The incident ultimately infected around one million MySpace profiles.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles were infected, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The Biba model is identified as a key security model that adds integrity verification on top of access control.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms Biba adds integrity verification but does not state it is a key security model or that it builds on access control.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The access control matrix is described as a basic control structure for implementing access policies.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that ACM is a basic control structure, matching the marking point's claim.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The matrix offers clarity of definition as an advantage.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote explicitly lists 'clarity of definition' as an advantage, directly matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: An ACL is an object-centred description of access rights, illustrated by entries such as bill.doc granting Bob read and write.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms ACL is object-centered but does not include the illustrative example of bill.doc granting Bob read and write.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The IDS confirms whether an attack succeeded or failed by examining host-based IDS log entries.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that HIDS log entries verify the success or failure of an attack, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Misuse detection recognises known bad behaviour rather than unknown behaviour.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that misuse detection systems recognize known bad behavior, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Under the simple security rule, a subject may access an object only if it is within the Wall (same company datasets already accessed) or in an entirely different conflict of interest class.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote covers the 'within the Wall' condition but omits the alternative 'entirely different conflict of interest class' part of the rule.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The identification stage involves acquiring the biometric sample, creating the master characteristics and storing them.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote lists acquisition, creation of master characteristics, and storage of master characteristics as activities in the identification stage, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Iris scanning requires no physical touch and overcomes the issues associated with retinal scanners.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote supports the no-touch claim but says nothing about overcoming retinal scanner issues.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Fingerprint authentication suffers from disadvantages such as racial issues, dirt, grime and wounds, and placement of the finger.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote mentions only racial issues, one of several disadvantages listed in the marking point, and does not address dirt, grime, wounds, or finger placement.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Access control should be applied to the password files so that they are protected from unauthorised reading.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote states access control is applied to password files but does not mention protecting them from unauthorised reading.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the burden of remembering many passwords.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that single sign-on reduces the need to memorize passwords, matching the point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the time users spend typing passwords.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that single sign-on reduces time spent typing passwords, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: State the core principle of the Trusted Computing architecture, namely that each stage of the platform measures and validates the following stage.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that each stage measures and validates the next one, matching the core principle in the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Identify the sequence in which the chain proceeds, beginning with the hardware TPM and continuing through the RTM, the TPM software stack, the BIOS and the kernel.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms the chain begins with the hardware TPM and continues to software, but does not specify the RTM, TPM software stack, BIOS, and kernel sequence.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Describe the TPM as a tamper-resistant hardware module mounted in the platform that performs measurement, protected storage, integrity reporting and policy enforcement.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms the TPM is a tamper-resistant hardware module mounted in a platform but does not mention measurement, protected storage, integrity reporting, or policy enforcement.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Identify that NGSCB's two primary components are the Nexus (a special security kernel that authenticates and protects data) and the Nexus Computing Agent (NCA).
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote identifies the Nexus as a special kernel but does not mention the Nexus Computing Agent (NCA), so only part of the point is supported.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Note that Nexus provides the application interface to the TPM and does not trust the OS.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms Nexus provides the application interface to the TPM but does not state that it does not trust the OS.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: State that a code of ethics is a written record of the behaviours a professional or social group considers acceptable.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that a code is a documented set of acceptable behaviors for professional or social groups, matching the marking point.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Note that the ethical standards in the code are set by the group itself rather than imposed from outside.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote 'Defined by the group' directly states that the code's standards are set by the group itself rather than imposed externally.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Explain that the code classifies particular behaviours as either acceptable or unacceptable.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that the code identifies specific actions as appropriate or inappropriate, matching the point about classifying behaviours as acceptable or unacceptable.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Point out that a code may fail to capture the personal ethics held by some individuals within the group.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that a code may not reflect every member's ethics, matching the point about failing to capture some individuals' personal ethics.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Merely describing moral and ethical dimensions of ICT is insufficient; the team must actively address privacy concerns rather than only documenting them.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote supports that describing is insufficient but does not mention privacy concerns or the team actively addressing them.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The organisation can adopt a recognised professional body's code, such as the ACM code of ethics and professional conduct, as the basis for its privacy obligations.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms the ACM has a code of ethics and professional conduct but does not state that an organisation can adopt it as the basis for its privacy obligations.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: Professional bodies such as AITP support members through education and information on relevant IT issues, helping the team understand its privacy duties.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms education and information on relevant IT issues but does not mention AITP, professional bodies, or privacy duties specifically.

low_stem_overlap_points.point: The ACM maintains a code of ethics and professional conduct that the security team can follow when handling information responsibly.
low_stem_overlap_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms ACM has a code of ethics and professional conduct but does not state that the security team can follow it for handling information responsibly.

scenario_questions.scenario: A hospital is deploying a fleet of networked medical workstations and wants each machine to prove, at boot time, that only approved software is running before it is allowed onto the clinical network. The security team proposes basing this assurance on a hardware module fitted to every workstation.
